<interfaces>
<!-- The shipped facts to document (from plans 02-03) + the exact prior-art form + the gate to discharge. -->

Act-mode enablement (D-10): the daemon reads `~/.claude/.autopilot/config.json` each poll.
  Enable  : write `{"act": true}`  -> next poll (~10s) the daemon acts on all mapped CC_TMUX crossings.
  Disable : write `{"act": false}` (or delete the file) -> back to observe-only (the SAFE default). No launchctl reload either way.

The shipped send-keys form (D-08, RESEARCH §2-§3): `tmux send-keys -t %N -l "/compact"` -> ~0.4s settle
(ENTER_SETTLE_SECS) -> a SEPARATE `tmux send-keys -t %N Enter`. Bare `/compact`, no summary. Idle guard:
`tmux capture-pane -p -t %N` tail contains the prompt marker = idle/safe; else busy_skip.

New JSONL decisions (D-13, 7-field shape kept): compact_sent (fired), busy_skip (pane busy — retry next
poll), compact_deduped (a fresh nudge marker owned the compaction). Observe-only still logs would_compact.

The gate this discharges: INSTALL.md §6 (Phase 19) — "OPERATOR RESIDUAL (live >=60% crossing): confirm
exactly one would_compact is logged and NO /compact is sent." Phase 20's gate is the ACT version: with
act on, confirm exactly one compact_sent, the session actually compacts, used_pct drops, no other pane touched.

RESEARCH §6 live-verify checklist (what the mock can't prove) — the operator runs these:
  1. send-keys -t %N -l "/compact" + 0.4s + Enter actually SUBMITS /compact (not absorbed as [Pasted text]).
  2. used_pct in $TMPDIR/claude-ctx-{id}.json DROPS afterward (the round-trip proof).
  3. the prompt-marker idle check reads true at an idle prompt, false mid-turn, on the live 2.1.18x TUI.
  4. no focus stolen, no other pane touched.
  5. whether bare /compact needs the 0.4s delay (keep it regardless).

NOTE: INSTALL.md already contains non-ASCII (the Phase-19 record uses box-drawing + the prompt glyph), so
every grep on INSTALL.md in this plan uses `grep -a` (BSD grep silently suppresses `-c`/`-n` on a file it
mis-classes as binary — the documented project trap).
</interfaces>
